newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Sipa tests show gold intersections.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Sipa tests show gold intersections.

text.p: Sipa Resources International NL said on Thursday that drill tests at its Ashburton mine project in Western Australia show significant gold intersections of up to 77 metres, grading five grammes of gold a tonne.

Separately, the Australian Stock Exchange said that Sipa's shares would resume trading on the exchange on Thursday following a suspension of trading on September 26, pending the release of an announcement to the market.
Sipa shares last traded at that date at 27 cents each.
In early trading, Sipa shares were up 11 cents at 38 cents.
The Ashburton project includes the Sipa's 15 percent-owned Dublin Hill farm-in agreement, in which it holds a right to earn a 55 percent stake in the intial exploration phase.

Sipa owns 100 percent of some 2,500 square kilometres of exploration licences in the region, it said. The Dublin Hill farm-in covers the Mount Olympus prospect, where it said it had had "very encouraging" results from drill tests.
These results include down-hole intervals from 17 metres, grading five grammes of gold/t, to 77 metres, grading five grammes of gold/t, the company said. -- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
